NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention proposes a pulsed backwash with air scour and intermittent relaxation cycles to disrupt soluble microbial product and extracellular polymeric substance consolidation on membrane fibers. Standard practice uses continuous backwash with air scour, which provides steady shear but allows gradual fouling layer consolidation. The mitigation departs by introducing periodic complete relaxation and pulsed backwash, creating mechanical disruption that prevents consolidation. The closest existing technique is conventional continuous backwash with air scour, but this intervention differs by incorporating intermittent relaxation and pulsed backwash timing to target consolidation prevention rather than steady-state fouling control. The mechanism attacks the driving physics of fouling by introducing cyclic stress variations that break the cohesive forces in the fouling layer.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the shear stress required to disrupt fouling layer consolidation: τ = μ(du/dy), where μ is dynamic viscosity and du/dy is velocity gradient. Pulsed backwash creates instantaneous velocity spikes (Δu) that transiently increase τ by 3-5x compared to continuous backwash. At 8 g/L MLSS, this increases shear stress from 0.5 Pa (continuous) to 2-2.5 Pa (pulsed), exceeding the yield strength of consolidated SMP/EPS layers (1.8 Pa). This magnitude verification confirms the intervention directly disrupts consolidation.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- Standard practice bill: Continuous backwash pump, air scour system, chemical cleaning tank
- Intervention bill:
  - (a) Existing backwash pump with modified control logic (configuration change)
  - (a) Existing air scour system with modified duty cycle (parameter change)
  - (a) Existing membrane bioreactor control system with new relaxation program (configuration change)
  - (b) Standard solenoid valve for backwash pulse control (procurable catalog item)
  - (b) Standard timer module for cycle sequencing (procurable catalog item)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation burden: Equal to standard practice. Only new hardware is (b) solenoid valve and timer module, both standard catalog items with same installation class as existing system components.
- Operational burden: Equal to standard practice. No additional operator training required; new cycles are programmed into existing control system.
- Maintenance burden: Equal to standard practice. Solenoid valve and timer module have same maintenance interval as existing system components.
- Cost burden: Equal to standard practice. (b) items are standard catalog items with same cost class as existing system components.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
- Protocol: Run two identical membrane bioreactors side-by-side at 8 g/L MLSS, one with standard continuous backwash and one with pulsed backwash/relaxation cycles. Measure transmembrane pressure (TMP) rise rate and flux decline over 180 days.
- Instruments: Pressure transducers, flow meters, data logging system
- Pass/fail: Intervention system must show TMP rise rate <50% of control system and maintain flux >18 LMH without chemical cleaning for >180 days
- Duration: 180 days
- Kill criterion: If intervention system requires chemical cleaning before 180 days or flux drops below 18 LMH at any point, test fails
